guidance.sentence: • Raising full year 2026 MRD revenue guidance to a new range of $268 million to $278 million, implying annual growth of 26% to 31%.
Adaptive Biotechnologies expects full year revenue for the MRD business to be between $268 million and $278 million, updated from the previous range between $260 million and $270 million.
We expect full year total company operating expenses, including cost of revenue, to be between $350 million and $355 million, updated from the previous range between $350 million and $360 million.

writeup.headline: Adaptive Biotechnologies rates Hold: strong trend and cash pile offset by a steep valuation and losses.
writeup.thesis: Adaptive scores 51, a Hold, because strengths and weaknesses roughly cancel out. The share price trend scores 96, with the price 45.4% above its 200-day average and shares 100.6 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days. The balance sheet scores 100, with no debt and 14.3 years of cash at the current burn. Growth scores 65 on TTM revenue growth of 50.1%, though growth slowed by 13.6 pp from the previous quarter to latest-quarter revenue growth of 21.5% year on year. Quality scores 28, with an operating margin of -12.2% and stock-based pay at 15.9% of revenue. Valuation scores 3: a price-to-sales ratio of 14.7x is high in absolute terms, and P/S is more expensive than at 49 of the last 51 month-ends.
key_risks: Valuation risk: P/S of 14.7x is high in absolute terms, and the FCF yield is 5.5 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, so any disappointment could hit the shares hard after a big run.
Slowing growth: growth slowed by 13.6 pp from the previous quarter, and Q3 results are due on November 4, 2026.
Final CMS 2027 lab fee schedule rates, due in November, could cut clonoSEQ pricing.
Continued losses and dilution: operating margin of -12.2%, FCF margin of -7.8% and diluted share count up 5.1% year on year.
Steady insider selling by the President and COO and the CCO for MRD, with no insider purchases.
what_would_change: Up to Buy (14 points away at 65): quality would need to improve, for example operating and FCF margins turning toward positive, while growth holds up.
Down to Sell (7 points below, under 45): a fading trend score after the strong run, or a further slowdown in growth, could push the score below 45.
Q3 results on November 4 and the final CMS pricing decision could move the growth and news risk scores either way.
